Root.render.notes: The documented way to make a group label: <Fieldset.Root render={<RadioGroup />}> or render={<CheckboxGroup />}. When render is a RadioGroup/Slider the underlying <fieldset> is replaced, which is how Fieldset provides group labelling + form integration.

Legend.className/style/render.type: string | fn / CSSProperties | fn / ReactElement | fn
Legend.className/style/render.notes: Legend renders a <div> (verified in FieldsetLegend.mjs -> useRenderElement('div', ...)), not a native <legend>, so it can be styled freely.

dataAttributes: No data-* attributes are documented for Fieldset.Root or Fieldset.Legend

renderProp.elementForm: <Fieldset.Root render={<RadioGroup defaultValue="ssd" />}> — the canonical group-labelling composition

formIntegration.note: Renders a real <fieldset> by default (verified: useRenderElement('fieldset', ...)), so it participates in native disabled-fieldset semantics. Legend renders a <div> and is wired as the accessible name for the grouped controls.

notableDifferences: React Aria folds group labelling into each component (e.g. RadioGroup label prop / Fieldset-like wrappers); Base UI makes Fieldset.Root the single group-labelling primitive and composes it onto RadioGroup/CheckboxGroup through render.
Legend renders a <div>, not a native <legend>, so the native legend layout/behaviour differences disappear.
Fieldset.Root state is only { disabled } — there is no data-valid/data-invalid set here.
